sources.title: Burundi Colline Climate Resilience Project (P180864): Appraisal Environmental and Social Review Summary
sources.temporal_coverage: Appraisal-stage project context and proposed activities, 2024
sources.methodology: World Bank appraisal summarizes cited colline climate-risk mapping, targeting and proposed activities.
sources.limitations: Activities are proposed; cited risk analyses are summarized, not replicated.

sources.title: Climate Change, Internal Mobility, and Conflict Dynamics: Country Brief - Burundi
sources.temporal_coverage: Survey interviews May-July 2025; displacement experiences within the previous five years
sources.methodology: Original country brief analyzing 1,027 in-person 4Mi surveys with internally displaced people, collected in Bujumbura city, Cibitoke and Makamba city.
sources.limitations: Purposive sample focused on recent climate-linked movement and active mobility; results are illustrative, not representative. Cover date is April 2026, while the suggested citation inside the report says 2025.

sources.title: Burundi country strategic plan (2024-2027)
sources.temporal_coverage: Country strategic plan period 2024-2027; revision approved June 2026
sources.methodology: WFP country strategic plan page describing climate and food-security context, planned outcomes and government capacity support.
sources.limitations: The page states commitments and intended outcomes; it does not evaluate whether planned support has been delivered or caused results.

claims.locator: PDF p. 4, environmental and social setting
claims.paraphrase: World Bank appraisal identifies 347 rural collines as very-high climate/environmental-fragility hotspots, concentrated in western and eastern Burundi.
claims.limitations: The appraisal does not name all 347 collines.

claims.paraphrase: The proposed project targets 71 locations covering 65 hotspot collines across seven provinces, including Cibitoke, Gitega, Kirundo, Kayanza, Bujumbura and Muyinga.
institutions: Ministry of Environment, Agriculture and Livestock
claims.limitations: The seventh province label is unclear and remains unnormalized; targets are proposed.

claims.locator: PDF p. 5, social and environmental context
claims.paraphrase: The appraisal states that heavier rainfall and landslides degrade scarce land and can heighten tensions, weaken cohesion and reopen post-conflict trauma.
claims.limitations: National pathway; frequency and climate contribution are unquantified.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: It links climate-intensified heavy rain/landslides to land loss and tension in a post-conflict setting (PDF p. 5).

claims.locator: PDF pp. 3-4, proposed community livelihood-resilience component
claims.paraphrase: Proposed measures include colline climate-action plans, local early warning and contingency systems, livelihood diversification, and land certification.
claims.limitations: Appraisal-stage intentions; implementation outcomes are not reported.

claims.locator: PDF p. 4, key findings; PDF p. 9, methodology
claims.paraphrase: Among 1,027 purposively selected climate-affected IDPs interviewed in Bujumbura, Cibitoke and Makamba in 2025, 63% reported flood impacts, 34% landslides and 34% unpredictable weather.
claims.limitations: The sample focused on recent climate-linked movement and is not representative of all displaced people in Burundi.

claims.locator: PDF p. 12, reported flood impacts and movement triggers
claims.paraphrase: Among surveyed IDPs affected by floods, 96% said housing destruction or damage prompted movement; 22% also cited household food or water scarcity.
claims.limitations: Reported triggers are self-reported by a purposive survey sample; they do not estimate national displacement shares.

claims.locator: PDF p. 17, early warning and adaptation findings
claims.paraphrase: In the purposive sample, 91% reported no early-warning system. Of 92 respondents who received some warning, 37% could not act because of limited resources; crop and livestock adaptation were uncommon and often ineffective.
claims.limitations: Purposive, short-period sample; percentages are sample-specific.

claims.locator: HTML page, plan context and outcomes 3-5
claims.paraphrase: WFP's June 2026 plan revision commits to climate-sensitive livelihoods and social-protection support, especially for women smallholders, and to strengthening government food-system, assistance and coordination capacity.
claims.limitations: This is a plan commitment, not evidence of delivered services or measured effects.

access_audit.notes: Opened and read the appraisal summary, proposed interventions, local targeting and contextual fragility passage.
Read findings, sampling/limitations and early-warning/adaptation sections; updated province boundary change is noted by the source.

access_audit.locator: HTML page, country context and outcomes
access_audit.notes: Opened the current country plan page and read the June 2026 revision status and outcomes.
Public PDF search result carried an Official Use Only mark despite public-disclosure labels; excluded to avoid relying on potentially restricted material.

search_audit.query: Burundi climate subnational vulnerability colline province landscape soil erosion local livelihoods public report
search_audit.outcome: Located and opened World Bank colline project appraisal material and MMC's survey brief; both identify localized risk and displacement evidence.

search_audit.query: Burundi explicit climate change conflict fragility mediator land farmer herder source report
search_audit.outcome: World Bank appraisal text explicitly links rainfall/landslide degradation of scarce land with community tensions in a post-conflict setting; no stronger quantified local conflict estimate was found in inspected sources.

search_audit.query: Burundi conflict insecurity reverse effect climate adaptation displacement agricultural resilience report
search_audit.outcome: Reviewed MMC field findings and WFP plan; no direct source-stated evidence was found that current conflict restricts household climate adaptation beyond the documented post-conflict context and displacement barriers.

search_audit.query: Burundi local resilience capacity climate adaptation institutions community public evaluation report
search_audit.outcome: World Bank appraisal describes proposed local land certification and early warning; MMC documents low warning access and resource-constrained responses; WFP plan records intended government and livelihood support.

gaps: Available evidence supports climate-related internal displacement and a source-stated scarce-land/social-cohesion pathway, but current conflict-specific constraints on household adaptation were not established.
The MMC sample was purposive and concentrated in Bujumbura and Cibitoke; the source warns it is not representative of national mobility dynamics.
The World Bank project document is an appraisal-stage design, so its local capacity measures remain planned rather than evaluated.
